# ctables/syscall

> System call: `syscall(n, args...)` with up to six arguments.

truck [ctables](../ctables.md) · [source](../../../registry/ctables/syscall.pkg) · translates [std/syscall](../std/syscall.md)

  Goes through the C library's `syscall`, and turns its `-1` and `errno`
  back into the negative error number that Linux returns, so programs see
  the same results as with bintables. The arguments are evaluated right to
  left, like bintables. Syscall numbers are the x86-64 Linux ones.

## Emit variants

The first variant whose condition holds is used.

### `emit when args count 1`

```nasm
({
{each args reverse}
W {it.L.v} =
{it}
;
{end}
__pk_syscall(0
{each args}
, {it.L.v}
{end}
, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0); })
```

## Support code (once per program)

```nasm
static W __pk_syscall(W _, W n, W a, W b, W c, W d, W e, W f) {
long r = syscall(n, a, b, c, d, e, f);
return r == -1 ? -(W)errno : (W)r;
}
```
